newsitem.title: BELARUS: Thousands rally in Minsk against Belarus president.
newsitem.headline: Thousands rally in Minsk against Belarus president.

text.p: Thousands of people rallied in the Belarussian capital Minsk on Saturday to oppose President Alexander Lukashenko and his bid to extend his powers.
The crowd of opposition leaders, nationalists and ordinary people from all over the former Soviet republic on Russia's western flank were expressing their anger at Lukashenko's pro-Moscow policies.
Chants of "Long live Belarus!" and "Down with Lukashenko!" filled the central streets as the columns of people marched by.

City authorities played recorded messages warning the crowd that their gathering had not been officially cleared. But police said they would not intervene as long as protesters did not disrupt public order.
Lukashenko has infuriated nationalists with his dismissive comments about the little-used Belarussian language and his policy of forming some kind of union with Russia.
The crowds were demonstrating in particular against an "All-Belarus Congress" called by the 42-year-old president for later on Saturday to back a November 7 referendum broadening his authority.

The vote would allow him to extend his term, due to expire in 1999, by more than two years without election and to appoint all court judges and half the Constitutional Court and central electoral commission.

Parliament has refused to approve the poll and instead has called another vote for November 24 -- which, among other questions, asks the nation of 10 million people if the presidency should be scrapped.
Thousands of mostly young Belarussians have filled the streets of Minsk 10 times this year in anti-Lukashenko protests which have at times turned violent and led to hundreds of arrests.
